stories.headline: General Dynamics beats Q2 EPS/revenue, raises FY guidance, posts record $136.5B backlog; shares still fall with defense-sector rotation
stories.one_line: GD Q2 EPS $4.24 (beat $3.95 consensus, +13.4% YoY); revenue $14.09B (beat $13.49B, +8.1% YoY); Aerospace +15.1% YoY, Marine Systems +10.4% YoY; record backlog $136.5B (+32% YoY); FY guidance raised. Shares still fell 3.00% today amid broad defense-sector valuation-compression rotation, not a company-specific concern.
stories.score_note: Clean beat-and-raise falling anyway supports a rotation, not fundamentals, read on today's defense-sector weakness.

stories.headline: Broadest single-session risk-off move this week: Dow -2.2%, S&P -1.5%, VIX +10.1% as FOMC dissent, Iran escalation and pre-earnings positioning combine
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (this run's own Yahoo Finance/Cboe fetch, primary)
stories.one_line: All major indices closed sharply lower (Dow -2.19%, S&P -1.51%, Nasdaq -1.74%, Russell -1.60%). VIX +10.10% to 20.05, still ordinary contango. TLT -1.65% to a new 52-week low. AI-infrastructure (Vertiv -17.2% post-earnings, Micron -9.9%) and small-cap defense/space names (Kratos -9.8%, York Space -15.7%, Voyager -11.8%) hit hardest, several without a confirmed company-specific catalyst. Energy (XLE +1.85%) and exchange operators (CBOE, CME, ICE) were the session's few gainers.
stories.score_note: Combines three distinct catalysts into the sharpest broad selloff tracked this week; small-cap defense/space weakness exceeds what broad risk-off alone explains.
sources: this run's own Yahoo Finance and Cboe fetches (primary)

stories.headline: Kumamoto death-toll dispute widens: NPR reports 18 dead with detailed casualty breakdown vs the multiply-corroborated 13
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple on 13; Disputed vs a well-sourced 18 figure (NPR)
stories.one_line: This morning tracked 13 confirmed dead with one outlet (KSAT) citing 18 unreconciled. NPR has now published a detailed 18-dead account: a Nippon Paper Industries chimney collapse killed 5 (7 rescued), and 8 were pulled from a partially collapsed shopping mall "torn apart by an apparent explosion" about an hour after the quake; 62+ injured, 6 seriously. Other wires (ABC, Rappler, GPB) still cite 13. Semiconductor impact remains contained; Mitsubishi Electric still silent.
stories.score_note: Death-toll discrepancy widens rather than resolves; new mall-explosion detail warrants follow-up.

stories.headline: AI-chip and power-infrastructure selloff extends into a third session as Korean chipmakers fall further overnight
stories.one_line: Korea's KOSPI fell nearly 6% overnight (Yahoo Finance market-today coverage), extending Tuesday's US-session declines (AMD -8.15%, Micron -8.85%, Marvell -7.77%, this terminal's own EWY proxy -6.05%). US index futures point to continued rotation, not broadening: NQ=F roughly flat (-0.01% vs last evening's confirmed print), ES=F/RTY=F modestly higher, YM=F modestly lower. NVDA itself remained little-changed Tuesday (+0.25%). Tonight's Microsoft/Meta/Arm/Qualcomm earnings are the next concrete test.
stories.score_note: Third consecutive session of Asian AI-chip weakness; durability question now tied directly to tonight's mega-cap capex guidance.
sources: this run's own Yahoo Finance futures/equity fetch (primary)

stories.headline: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% with historic 3-way hawkish dissent (first since 2016) as Warsh rejects a "pause" framing
stories.one_line: FOMC voted 9-3 to hold; Dallas Fed's Logan, Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari and Cleveland Fed's Hammack all dissented for a 25bp hike, the first unified three-way hawkish dissent since Sept 2016. Warsh's 2:30 PM press conference used his "family fight" framing and explicitly rejected characterizing the hold as a pause. Forecast 2026-07-29-am-1 (hike, 25-35% probability) resolves wrong; graded Saturday.
stories.score_note: Resolves the week's highest-importance scheduled event; market reaction (broad equity selloff, yields modestly higher) treated as a hawkish surprise.

stories.headline: Trump vows to "hit Iran hard"; Tehran details (unverified) war damage including Bushehr Airport and 350 employees killed; IRGC keeps striking Iraqi Kurdistan
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (Trump quotes); Unverified (Iranian government damage claims)
stories.one_line: Following this morning's Jordan missile attack, Trump told Fox News the US would "hit Iran hard." Iranian government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani gave a cumulative damage accounting (Bushehr Airport out of service, ~230M cubic meters lost gas capacity, ~350 government employees killed) that Reuters could not independently verify. Separately, IRGC continued a distinct campaign of drone/missile strikes on Iranian-Kurdish opposition bases in Iraq's Kurdistan region (14+ strikes since Monday), a related but separate front. No confirmed new US strike on Iran itself as of this run.
stories.score_note: Highest-risk geopolitical thread; gap between Trump's retaliation vow and any confirmed new strike is itself notable.

stories.headline: Iran-Ukraine Caspian incident continues: lawmaker's fresh retaliation threat, Ukraine defends the strike, Israel still silent
stories.one_line: No new strike or retaliatory action. Iranian lawmaker Ebrahim Azizi (distinct from FM Araghchi) separately warned Ukraine that 'Iran does not leave its actions unanswered.' Ukraine's ambassador to Israel defended the strike, calling the vessel's cargo (drone/missile components) 'legitimate military targets.' Neither Israel nor Ukraine has addressed Araghchi's unevidenced 'at Israel's behest' claim, unchanged from this morning.
stories.score_note: Escalation risk for the broader Iran conflict, entangled with Russia-Ukraine; watch for Iranian action.

stories.headline: Supreme Court sets Aug 3 deadline on mail-ballot EO stay; separate D.C. Circuit ruling finds a related challenge premature
stories.one_line: Justice Jackson (1st Circuit circuit justice) declined an immediate administrative stay and set a 4:00pm Aug 3 response deadline for respondent states -- a scheduling order, not a merits ruling (several outlets' 'denied' framing overstates this). Separately, a D.C. Circuit panel unanimously affirmed a different challenge to the same EO was not yet ripe (USPS hasn't issued implementing regulations), voicing skepticism about the administration's authority and feasibility before November; does not affect the pending SCOTUS stay application.
stories.score_note: Live emergency Supreme Court matter with a stated response deadline; procedural progress on two fronts, no merits ruling yet.

stories.headline: Microsoft, Meta, Arm and Qualcomm report after today's close; results pending as of this report's cutoff
stories.one_line: All four remain scheduled to report after today's close per Microsoft's own investor-relations page; no results published as of this report's 16:30 ET cutoff. FY27 capex guidance remains the framed swing factor for the AI-infrastructure trade. Tomorrow's Morning Brief covers results and after-hours reaction.
stories.score_note: Direct test of whether today's AI-infrastructure selloff reflects durable repricing or a temporary rotation.

stories.headline: Hugging Face publishes full reconstruction of the OpenAI agent breach; AI agent finds two critical Microsoft Bing vulnerabilities
stories.one_line: Hugging Face's security team recovered ~17,600 attacker actions clustered into ~6,280 operations from the Jul 9-13 incident -- the clearest data-backed account yet. Separately, an autonomous offensive-security AI agent identified two critical (CVSS 9.8) Microsoft Bing vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-32194, CVE-2026-32191). The Agentic AI Foundation released an updated MCP spec (2026-07-28), the largest change since launch.
stories.score_note: Upgrades the tracked breach story from narrative to granular data; Bing CVE discovery is a new dual-use AI-security data point.

stories.headline: Coca-Cola/Anubis leak confirmed resolved (forecast correct); Abbott Laboratories confirms two new cyber incidents amid ShinyHunters claims
stories.verification: Confirmed-primary (Abbott's own confirmation, Coca-Cola's own confirmation); claimed data volumes Unverified
stories.one_line: Anubis's leak of ~1TB Fairlife data is confirmed to have occurred, resolving forecast 2026-07-27-pm-1 (leak within 72h, 45-60% probability) as correct; graded Saturday. Separately, Abbott Laboratories confirmed two cyber incidents: unauthorized access to legacy Exact Sciences systems, and a separate LabCentral portal breach claim. ShinyHunters says it used a mid-June vishing campaign to compromise a Microsoft Entra SSO account, claiming 30M+ records (22M+ doctor-patient notes, 20M+ medical orders); neither group has published a data sample. EY's ShinyHunters deadline (Jul 31) unchanged.
stories.score_note: New healthcare-sector breach adds to the ongoing extortion-campaign thread; vishing-based SSO compromise is a notable vector.

stories.headline: Arista ships VeloCloud patches ahead of CISA deadline; Origin Energy attacker claims unconfirmed settlement
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (Arista, CISA) / Unverified (Origin Energy settlement claim)
stories.one_line: Arista shipped patched VeloCloud Orchestrator versions (CVE-2026-16812); CISA's federal deadline remains Jul 30, exploitation continuing. CISA separately added a second Fortinet FortiOS flaw (CVE-2025-68686) to KEV, deadline Aug 10. On Origin Energy (~900,000-customer breach): the claimed attacker told an Australian outlet a private settlement was reached and no data will leak; Origin has not confirmed this -- treated as an unverified attacker claim.
stories.score_note: Patch-compliance and breach-settlement threads to watch this week.

stories.one_line: No new information found this run; forecast 2026-07-27-am-2 (1.0-2.5% range) stands.
stories.score_note: Critical scheduled macro release, one day after FOMC.

stories.one_line: Fed's preferred wage-inflation gauge, closes out the week's data calendar. No new information this run.
stories.score_note: High-importance scheduled macro release.

stories.headline: Starship heat-shield durability questioned by former NASA researchers as SPCX slides to a fresh 52-week low ahead of Aug 6 lockup
stories.one_line: Bloomberg reports three former NASA researchers warn Starship's heat shield may substantially delay SpaceX's rapid-reuse ambitions. SPCX fell 3.32% to $112.55, a new 52-week low, roughly 15.9% below its 20-day moving average, continuing a pattern analysts attribute more to the approaching Aug 6 lockup expiration (~911.5M shares, ~1.4x float) than to any single day's news.
stories.score_note: Technical critique lands during a stock slide ahead of a major share-lockup unlock; worth tracking independent of short-term price action.
sources: this run's own Yahoo Finance quotes (primary)

stories.headline: OpenAI reportedly weighing IPO delay to 2027; Anthropic pushing toward an October 2026 debut
stories.one_line: No new IPO-timeline statement found for either company today. Both remain private; no valuation figures asserted (registry policy). (2026-07-29: reporting continues to describe OpenAI's CFO/CEO split on Sept 2026 vs 2027 timing, citing SpaceX's post-listing pullback as a cautionary signal; Anthropic still targeting late-2026. Valuation figures cited vary by source; registry's already-verified figures retained.)
stories.score_note: Registry-relevant; private-module entity status watch.

stories.headline: Fresh heat wave threatens France/Spain wildfire containment; evacuation estimates widen, Greece/Italy flagged as potentially next
stories.one_line: A new heat wave (up to 104F/40C) arrived today, raising re-ignition risk on already-dry landscape; evacuation figures vary materially by source this run (roughly 63,000 near Madrid to 200,000+ across the broader zone), not reconciled. Greece and Italy flagged as potentially next per NPR/UPI.
stories.score_note: Upgraded from steady-state to active re-escalation risk.

stories.headline: Bipartisan FRONTIER Act introduced in House to regulate catastrophic-risk AI models
stories.one_line: No committee markup or hearing today; hearings still expected once the House returns from its district work period in late August.
stories.score_note: First bipartisan House frontier-AI safety bill of this scope this session; intersects with mega-cap AI-capex earnings week.

stories.headline: NDAA FY2027: stalled in Senate; an unverified '77-20 passage' claim explicitly rejected
stories.one_line: No new Senate floor action found today; last confirmed activity was Thune withdrawing a renewed motion to proceed Jul 23 (per CRS). A single AI-search-surfaced claim of a '77-20' Senate passage could not be corroborated against Congress.gov/CRS records and is not adopted as fact. (2026-07-29: confirmed no new floor action since the House's Jul 22 216-212 passage; still stalled in the Senate on a filibuster threat per Majority Leader Thune. Dropped from Top Stories.)
stories.score_note: Direct relevance to defense/aerospace watchlist via program authorizations.

stories.headline: Minnesota AG responds to injunction blocking prediction-market ban; no appeal filed yet
stories.one_line: Minnesota AG Keith Ellison publicly responded to Monday's federal injunction, calling prediction markets 'gambling, plain and simple' and confirming the state will keep defending the law; no notice of appeal reported yet.
stories.score_note: Sector-relevant regulatory thread for prediction-market operators; indirect COIN/HOOD relevance via adjacent market structure.

stories.headline: Berlin Pride attack: no material change since second suspect's release
stories.one_line: Second detained suspect remains released; no new investigative developments found this run. Additional suspects not ruled out.
stories.score_note: International public-safety story, ongoing legal process; low direct US-market relevance.
